summary: Refresh eligibility for a desktop token source is decided from what is on disk, never from an assumption about which file is the modern one. Whenever supabase.json.enc exists, the stored-accounts.json fallback is desktop-owned and D6 applies to it: read it, never rotate it. Refresh stays allowed only on installs that never had an encrypted store, where the plaintext file genuinely is legacy.
reason: An earlier deferral called stored-accounts 'rarely populated on modern installs' and left it refresh-allowed. Granola's key migration inverted that premise — with supabase.json.enc unreadable, the loader falls through to stored-accounts on exactly the installs people use. WorkOS refresh tokens are single-use, so rotating the desktop's copy signs the user out of Granola desktop.
